title: Record that somebody played the web build before a tag
ask: Nothing records that anybody played the exported web build before a tag, so the runbook's first pre-release box measures only whether somebody ticked a box. Design the smallest honest record: an attestation keyed to the tag being cut, so it expires with each release instead of standing forever, and wire it into the launch check on the Sales & Platforms page.
first_action: Read docs/DEPLOY.md's 'Before any release' section and hq/data/goals/sales.json, then propose the record's shape.
source_message: Nothing records that anybody played the exported web build before a tag, so the runbook's first pre-release box measures only whether somebody ticked a box. Design the smallest honest record: an attestation keyed to the tag being cut, so it expires with each release instead of standing forever, and wire it into the launch check on the Sales & Platforms page.
result:
The gate that said "nobody is checking this" now has a record behind it, and a way for you to make one.

**What the record is.** A new file, `hq/data/attestations.json`, holds one entry per human act that no file can measure. Each entry names three things: the tag it was made for, the commit the build came from, and the date. Those first two are what make it perish. Cutting the tag spends the record — the next release wants a different tag, and no entry exists for it. And it lapses early if anything a player would meet changes after you played: the game folders, the assets, the project file. Changes to docs, tests or the dashboard don't touch it, so ordinary work doesn't keep knocking the row over.

**How you make one.** The Sales & Platforms page's row "Somebody played the actual web build end to end before it went out" now carries a button. First press arms it and states what you'd be claiming; second press writes the record. The server stamps the tag, the commit and the date — not the page, and not you by hand, because those are the three things a person gets wrong and the three things that make the entry worth anything. Today the row reads "nobody has played the build Player Update 1 would ship". After you press it, "you played it on 2026-09-04, on the build Player Update 1 would ship", and beside it, "holds until v0.2.0 is cut, or until the game changes under it". If the game moves under you it goes back to needing you, saying "the game has changed 3 times since".

Only you can attest — same rule the dashboard already applies to its one other attested row. The rest of the org are personas and a persona vouching for a thing nobody measured would be inventing studio activity.

**Two things you should know.** The runbook's box said "play the web build" without saying which one — the tag is what builds and publishes the web export, so before a tag there is nothing public to play. The runbook now says to export one locally from the commit you're about to tag and serve it over HTTP, which is two remembered steps I'd rather were one command. And nothing stops a tag that has no record; the credits and playtest-readout boxes below it are enforced by the release workflow, this one is not. Both are named in the follow-ups.

Both suites are green (1983 and 528 passing). The work is in the worktree, uncommitted, as the house rules require — nothing pushed.

check.summary: The perishable record, the button, and the runbook wording all landed as asked; what to watch is that the owner's proof of it working is the Godot suites, which never touch a line of this change, and one runbook line now contradicts the box beneath it.

findings.what: The reply's evidence measures the wrong thing: the two Godot suites (1983 and 528) exercise no file in this diff, and the exact row texts quoted as what Daniel would see are not reported as observed on a rendered page or a real button press
findings.where: hq/server.py (eval_measure attestation branch) and hq/static/pillars.js wireAttestButtons
findings.fix: Owner renders #/pillar/sales once, presses the button against a throwaway record, checks the three states (no record, holds, lapsed after a game-path commit), then reports that instead of the suite counts

findings.what: The runbook now contradicts itself: the manual export is introduced as 'if ever needed without a tag' six lines above a box that requires it before every tag
findings.fix: Reword the bullet to say it is the standard pre-tag step, or move the command into the box

findings.what: The record stamps HEAD and the lapse check counts commits only, so a build played from a dirty working tree is recorded against a commit it was not, and uncommitted game changes after the play never lapse it; the reply's 'lapses early if anything a player would meet changes' is stronger than the code
findings.where: hq/server.py record_attestation and the rev-list drift check
findings.fix: Refuse to attest when git status shows changes under code_paths, or record a dirty flag and treat it as lapsed
